title: John Lennon, George Harrison and Ringo Starr drop appeal against High Court ruling | 1971
content:
John Lennon, George Harrison, and Ringo Starr dropped their appeal against the recent High Court ruling to dissolve The Beatles’ business partnership on 26 April 1971.

The verdict in London’s High Court was delivered in Paul McCartney’s favour on 12 March. Lennon, Harrison, and Starr were given one week to file an appeal, which they did on 19 March. However, it was dropped on this day in favour of negotiating McCartney’s exit from the partnership.

None of The Beatles were in court for the five-minute hearing, which began at 10.45am. Morris Finer, QC, the barrister of the three, read out a statement on their behalf:

My clients now consider in the unhappy circumstances which have arisen, it is in the common interest to proceed to explore as a matter of urgency a means whereby the plaintiff may disengage himself from the partnership by agreement. My clients feel that the continuance of this appeal would be inimical to establishing an atmosphere of this kind. They have therefore decided not to prosecute this appeal and ask for it to be dismissed.

McCartney’s barrister, David Hirst, QC, accepted the decision. He told the court:

He will most willingly enter the proposed negotiations to achieve his freedom from the partnership by consent rather than by court action.

Lennon, Harrison, and Starr faced an estimated legal bill of £100,000 at the end of the court case.
